You are a senior prop designer. You are drawing the PROPS of one world for a code-rendered video engine
that makes workplace training and explainer videos for adults. They must match the sets of this world drawn in the

FORMAT
- One SVG per prop, viewBox sized to the prop with 16 px of margin, the prop standing on its base line; mark the base
  with <circle id="anchor_base" r="2" fill="none"/> and any grip, screen or top with anchor_ circles.
- Groups: <g id="base"> for the shapes, and classed groups as in the set contract: lm-shadow (a contact shadow under
  the prop only), lm-light, lm-texture, lm-outline, lm-hi, lm-glow as the style uses them.
- Moving parts (a laptop lid, clock hands, a door, a drawer, a monitor arm) as their own groups with a pivot anchor.
- Views: front and three-quarter for furniture and devices; one view for small things.
- No text, letters, numbers or logos (slots as empty rects); no images, filters or masks; up to 120 KB per prop.

STYLE: 2.5D LIT LAYERS (for cinematic moments, mood, emphasis: the camera pushes through depth and the light can change)
- A layout painter's room in vector layers: accurate two-point perspective, a clear value plan (light, middle, dark masses) before colour, and depth that the parallax camera can travel through.
- Every depth layer (far, mid, near) is split so the engine can relight it: the base shapes in local colour (outside the classed groups, as the contract says), then <g class="lm-shadow"> form and cast shadows, <g class="lm-light"> key-light shapes, <g class="lm-hi"> thin bright rim edges on silhouettes against the window, <g class="lm-atmos"> haze and light shafts.
- Materials read through light, not line: no outlines; edges come from value change. Glass reflects the window as one or two pale shapes; a satin floor shows a faint sheen under the window light, as a lighter low-opacity shape.
- Light setups are sibling groups inside each depth layer, each holding its own lm-shadow, lm-light, lm-hi and lm-atmos groups: id="setup_day" first (the main delivery: the scene's light). After I approve it, add id="setup_evening" (low sun, long shadows, lamps on) and id="setup_night" (window dark, lamps and screens are the lights) in the same file. The base shapes are shared. In this style a variant that only changes the light (evening, night) IS a setup, not a separate file; a variant that moves objects is a separate file.
- Paint what is behind every object: the wall and floor continue complete under the furniture of the mid and near layers, so a parallax move never shows a hole; the far layer runs past the frame into the overscan.
- Light: One warm key with believable cast shadows (window panes projected on the floor and table, stretched by perspective), a cool fill from the opposite side, light shafts as long transparent polygons in lm-atmos (2-stop linear gradients allowed there, light to transparent). Shadows are cool and coloured, never grey.
- Texture: Very little: a soft gradient across large walls in lm-atmos only. No noise.
- Depth: Aerial perspective: the far layer is lighter, cooler and lower in contrast, with haze over it at the amount the scene's Light paragraph states (0.3 to 0.45 for a deep space when it states none); the near layer is darkest and may be partly silhouetted against the light.
- Quality bar: A feature-animation colour key translated into clean vector layers: the light tells you the time of day and the mood before anything moves.

The plot, about 70 m by 45 m, sits inside a 2.4 m plywood hoarding along the street; at the entrance a vehicle gate and a separate pedestrian gate with a turnstile; beside them a two-storey stack of steel cabins (site office and induction room, canteen, drying room, toilets); between the cabins and the building a yard of crushed stone with fenced pedestrian routes, a materials area and new drainage trenches being dug across it.
